title: Forgiveness Sunday
hookLine: before Lent, Orthodox Christians ask forgiveness of one another

cards: The evening service is ending, but nobody leaves. Instead, the people form a line. The priest stands at the front, and one by one the congregation comes to him, and then to each other.
Each person stops in front of the next, bows, and says two words; then the other bows back. The grandmother and the teenager. The choir director and the man who complained about the choir.
Neighbors who haven't spoken since an argument over a fence. This is the Sunday before Lent in the Orthodox churches, and the Christians who keep it call it Forgiveness Sunday.

teach.b: First, the two words. In English, they're forgive me. The answer, in some parishes, is something like: God forgives, and I forgive.
The wording varies from place to place, but the shape stays: each person asks first. Second, why asking comes first.
It would be easy to walk down the line saying I forgive you, I forgive you, as if everyone else were the problem. The rite turns that around. Everyone asks, the person who was wronged too.
In a line like that, nobody gets to be only the injured party. Third, the Gospel behind it.
By tradition, the reading for this Sunday comes from Matthew, including the words: "For if ye forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you".
Then the passage turns to fasting: "Moreover when ye fast, be not, as the hypocrites, of a sad countenance".
Forgiveness first, then the fast. Fourth, why before Lent. Lent is a long season of fasting and prayer, and Orthodox Christians begin it the next day.
In this rite, peace with the people around you comes before the long fast. This path met the same order a few weeks back, in the gift left waiting at the altar. First the person in front of you.

how: On the Sunday before Great Lent, Orthodox Christians end the evening service with a rite of mutual forgiveness: each person bows to the others, asks forgiveness, and receives it.

games.q: you're in the line at the end of the service. the person in front of you is the one who hurt you this year. what do the words of the rite have you say first?
games.why: the rite has each person ask first: forgive me. the answer comes back: God forgives, and I forgive.

practice: Picture a line of people you know, family, friends, coworkers, standing quietly, and walk down it slowly in your mind.
At each face, don't decide who was right; just notice whether there's anything, even small, you'd ask forgiveness for, and when you find one, let the line stop.
Let the two words form silently, forgive me, and notice how they sit in the mouth; if you pray, you can bring that person and the words into your prayer.

wordCard.voice: Forgiveness Sunday. The Orthodox Christian day before Lent when people ask forgiveness of one another, face to face. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: forgive me. In that line everyone asks, even the one who was wronged. Until tomorrow.
